implementation.live_canary_success_rule: An active hourly cycle fetches public Kalshi open events/markets, writes a market_instance_scan artifact, records coverage/change counts, and routes bounded relation evidence without claiming net-positive EV before fees/L2/rule-exception review.

objective: Continuously inspect concrete Kalshi market instances and related contract families for logical, semantic and economically exploitable inconsistencies, independently of behavioral research and documentation-only reconnaissance.

scope.market_instances: active and newly listed markets first; recently changed or semantically related markets when needed for relation proof
relation_families: mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive partitions
same-event contracts expressed through different series or products
conditional, combo, MVE and multivariate payout relations
duplicate or near-duplicate contracts with potentially different settlement semantics

required_process: Capture market identity, event/series identity, rule text or authoritative settlement semantics, strike/range/window, close time and source provenance before inferring a relation.
Generate candidate relations from actual market instances rather than titles alone.
Prove the relation statewise from authoritative semantics before using any price discrepancy as evidence.
Classify relation as EQUIVALENT, DOMINATES, PARTITION, NESTED, MUTUALLY_EXCLUSIVE, COLLECTIVELY_EXHAUSTIVE, TEMPORAL_RELATION, SEMANTICALLY_DIFFERENT or UNPROVEN.
Only after semantic proof, compare synchronized executable bid/ask/L2, fees, rebates, depth, partial-fill risk, slippage, collateral and settlement horizon.
Treat UI probability, midpoint, last trade and title similarity as discovery clues only, never executable proof.
Preserve tested-negative relation families and concrete counterexamples so they are not rediscovered as new.
Every demonstrable net-positive executable opportunity remains research-worthy even if only cents per episode; scale affects ranking, not admission.
contradiction_checks: A and NOT-A executable costs inconsistent with guaranteed payout after fees
complete partition executable basket inconsistent with total guaranteed payout
nested market prices violate proven monotonic dominance
exact/range market differs from formally equivalent threshold portfolio
same statewise payoff has materially different executable cost across contract paths
a dominated contract is priced more favorably than its proven dominator in a way that survives execution frictions
time-window or deadline relations create impossible simultaneous outcomes or overlooked dominance
market metadata/title suggests identity but rules prove a hidden semantic mismatch
rule/market-instance interaction creates a contradiction not visible from documentation alone

recheck_triggers: new market instance in an existing relation family
changed close time, strike, bucket or measurement window

acceptance_criteria: Actual market instances are inspected, not only venue documentation or trader behavior.
Candidate relations are linked to concrete market IDs/tickers and point-in-time rule provenance.
No price contradiction is promoted before a formal semantic/statewise relation is established.
Executable economics uses synchronized bid/ask or L2 and all material frictions.
Valid but currently unprofitable or non-executable relations can remain WATCH with explicit triggers.
Existing PAYOFF-IDENTITY-MINING-V1 and negative-evidence records are reused rather than duplicated.
No candidate is discarded solely because the absolute profit opportunity is small.
No live trading, orders, wallet movement, paid actions or active security exploitation.
